records.derivation: Put s=BN and r=AN/BN>0. Median similarity gives CN=(r+2)*s: draw AY parallel to BX with Y on line CN opposite C; similar triangles give NY=r*s and the midpoint theorem gives NX=(CN-NY)/2=s. Write k=r+2. Cosine equations give BC²/s²=k²-k+1 and AC²/s²=r²+k²+r*k. The bisector ratio AC/BC=r leads to(r²-2)(r+1)(r+2)=0, so r=sqrt(2). Since AC=2, s²=4/(10+6*sqrt(2))=(10-6*sqrt(2))/7, choice A. The displayed coordinate route independently gives the same equations from distances and remains complete.

records.derivation: Normalize the equal side to s and radius to sqrt(2)*s. The general cosine law in the central isosceles triangle gives cos(theta)=3/4. Equal chords and inscribed angles give opposite quadrilateral angles theta and pi-theta. Hence the shared diagonal has square(7/2)*s². If the fourth side is u*s, the other triangle gives(7/2)=u²+1-(3/2)*u, or(2 u-5)(u+1)=0. The feasible u is 5/2, so AD=500, choice E. Independently, chord bisection gives h=100*sqrt(7), diagonal lengths 100*sqrt(14), and Ptolemy gives 200*AD=140000-40000, the same answer.
